$comment: Attribution for the COMPILED BINARIES this image adds on top of exeuntu (story DF2.10, AC5).
DF2.9's package sweep walks a node_modules tree and can say nothing about an ELF; this table is
the substance that discharges the obligation for those. It is NOT the coverage set: the set of
binaries that must appear here is COMPUTED by scripts/build-exedev-image.ts, which enumerates the
executables in the built image, enumerates them in the base image, diffs, and refuses to tag when
an added binary has no entry below. A table asserted against a list the table itself supplies is
tautological and would pass on an image carrying an unattributed binary.
The diff is BY PATH AND CONTENT: a built executable is 'added' when the base image has no file at
that path OR the base's bytes at that path differ (both listings are sha256'd, and the comparison
is `baseBins.get(p) !== sha`). So a binary the base already ships at the same path but whose bytes
we re-pin — pi, which exeuntu itself installs and this image re-installs at PI_VERSION — IS flagged
and MUST be attributed here. The pin is ours, so the attribution is ours, and the gate now says so
rather than relying on us to remember.
Known ceiling, stated rather than hidden, and it is on the COVERAGE side rather than the diff side:
an entry covers an added binary by BASENAME. 'paths' is the optional narrowing — when an entry
declares it, an added binary is covered only if its basename is in 'names' AND its full in-image
path is listed in 'paths' (in-image paths, no leading slash, matching the shape the executable
listing produces; present-but-empty or absolute is a validation failure, not a silent widening).
When 'paths' is absent the entry covers its basenames ANYWHERE in the image — exactly what every
entry did before the field existed, so the field narrows without invalidating an entry nobody has
re-measured. An entry without it would read /opt/vendor/bun as covered by a table that establishes
oven-sh/bun at /usr/local/bin; both entries below therefore declare 'paths', and a re-pin that
moves an install location must move them in the same change or the build refuses to tag.
Every TOP-LEVEL entry's 'spdxId' must resolve to a canonical text in oci/license-texts/ (the
build validates this with DF2.9's own resolveLicenseText). 'UNVERIFIED' is a legal value there
and is a BUILD FAILURE by design: it is how an unestablished license is recorded honestly
instead of guessed at.
The rule stops at the top level, deliberately and not by oversight. validateBinaryLicenses
requires only 'component', 'url' and 'note' of a 'bundled' member and does NOT resolve its
spdxId — which is what lets the LGPL-2.0-or-later and NOASSERTION entries below exist while no
LGPL text is checked in. Widening the canonical-text set to statically-linked components is
DF4.1's sweep. Stated here because the unscoped version of this sentence read as a guarantee
the build does not make.
CORRECTION to an earlier version of this note, which claimed a top-level 'NOASSERTION' is not
enforced. It IS enforced, and the two sentences above and below cannot both have been true. It
simply refuses by the ORDINARY path rather than the 'UNVERIFIED' special case: there is no
NOASSERTION.txt in oci/license-texts/ (and there could not sensibly be one), so resolveLicenseText
returns null and validateBinaryLicenses reports 'no canonical text in oci/license-texts/ for
"NOASSERTION"'. Different message, same build failure. Both spellings of 'we do not know' stop a
publish at the top level; only a 'bundled' member may carry NOASSERTION, because its spdxId is
never resolved. Verified against scripts/build-exedev-image.ts validateBinaryLicenses and
scripts/lib/license-sweep.ts resolveLicenseText, 2026-09-01.
Every URL below is pinned to the TAG of the artifact this image ships, never to blob/main/ — a
table that argues against mutable references cannot cite them. 'verifiedAt' pins the observation;
the tag pins the target. The one exception is the WebKit pointer, which is a bare repository URL
because that is exactly what bun's own LICENSE.md gives at the pinned tag; substituting a ref we
invented would be a worse pointer than upstream's.

entries.verifiedHow: PROVENANCE: 1.3.13 is oci/exedev/Dockerfile's ARG BUN_VERSION default, itself read from package.json `packageManager` by readBunPin and passed as --build-arg by scripts/build-exedev-image.ts, which also pins ARG BUN_SHA256 for that release's bun-linux-x64.zip. The ARG is overridable with --build-arg, so this field states the version of the PINNED build; an override that moves it must move this entry in the same change. LICENCE: 2026-08-31, fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oven-sh/bun/main/LICENSE.md — first line reads 'Bun itself is MIT-licensed.'; npm view bun@1.3.13 license = MIT. 2026-09-01, re-fetched at the TAG the Dockerfile downloads from, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oven-sh/bun/bun-v1.3.13/LICENSE.md — same first line, and it is that document (not main's) that names the static-link graph disclosed under 'bundled'.
entries.notes: 'bunx' is deliberately NOT listed: the Dockerfile installs exactly one file (`install -m 0755 bun-linux-x64/bun /usr/local/bin/bun`) and creates no bunx symlink, so naming it here claimed attribution for a binary this image does not ship. The coverage direction was safe — uncoveredBinaries diffs added-against-covered, so a name with no binary is inert — but the table is the legal artifact and attributedBinaries publishes its claims. Nothing in src/ or scripts/ invokes bunx in-box; if that changes, add the symlink to the Dockerfile AND the name back here, in the same re-pin. bun is MIT, but the SHIPPED BINARY statically links components under other licenses; they are disclosed in 'bundled' below rather than folded into spdxId, because spdxId names the license of the project we redistribute and a single identifier cannot honestly carry a static-link graph. GitHub's license API reports NOASSERTION for this repo for the same reason: LICENSE.md is a composite document, not a bare MIT text.

bundled.note: A bare repository URL, and deliberately so: it is verbatim what bun's own LICENSE.md at tag bun-v1.3.13 gives ('You can find the patched version of WebKit used by Bun here: <https://github.com/oven-sh/webkit>'), verified 2026-09-01. Upstream publishes no per-release ref for it, and inventing one would point at bytes nobody claims are the ones linked in. LGPL-2 clause (1) requires that a recipient be able to relink the application against a modified library. Discharged by the upstream instructions in bun's LICENSE.md plus the patched-WebKit source at the URL above. No LGPL text is checked into oci/license-texts/ — widening the canonical-text set to statically-linked components is DF4.1's sweep, not this story's, and pretending otherwise would mean shipping a NOTICE entry with no text behind it (DF2.9 INV-4).

bundled.component: boringssl, brotli, libarchive, lol-html, ls-hpack, ls-qpack, lsquic, mimalloc and further static libraries
bundled.note: Enumerated with per-library licenses in bun's own LICENSE.md (MIT / BSD-3-Clause / several-licenses). Recorded as a pointer, not transcribed: a transcription drifts on the next bun bump and a stale transcription is a worse attribution than a live reference. The pointer is pinned to the TAG this image ships, not to blob/main/ — 'a live reference' meant a reference that still describes THESE bytes, and main's LICENSE.md will one day enumerate a different static-link graph. Re-pin it in the same change that moves BUN_VERSION.

entries.verifiedHow: PROVENANCE: 0.84.4 is oci/exedev/Dockerfile's ARG PI_VERSION default, installed by `exeuntu update pi --home /home/exedev --version`. The ARG is overridable with --build-arg, so this field states the version of the PINNED build; an override that moves it must move this entry in the same change. Unlike bun there is NO content check on that install (no upstream checksum to pin), so the build records the sha256 of the installed binary in /etc/qds-image.json as `piSha256` — a record for drift detection, not a verification. LICENCE: the compiled ELF is NOT the npm package: npm @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent stops at 0.73.1 and has no 0.84.4, so the 0.55.0 manifest's `license: MIT` does not establish this artifact. Established instead at the release channel exeuntu actually pulls from — GitHub release earendil-works/pi v0.84.4 ships pi-linux-x64.tar.gz (the standalone binary the DF1.10 probe measured at /usr/local/bin/pi), and that repository's root LICENSE, fetched the same day, is the MIT text with 'Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner' (GitHub license API: spdx_id MIT). 2026-09-01, re-fetched AT THE TAG rather than at main — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/earendil-works/pi/v0.84.4/LICENSE opens 'MIT License' / 'Copyright (c) 2025 Mario Zechner', and https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/releases/tag/v0.84.4 resolves; a nonexistent tag returns 404 on both, so the 200 is the tag and not a soft redirect to the default branch.
entries.notes: exeuntu installs pi to /home/exedev/.local/bin/pi and symlinks /usr/local/bin/pi. `find -type f` sees the real file, not the symlink, so the added-binary diff keys on the former.
